lead: A bolted bracket rarely pulls through the centre of its bolt group. The load arrives off-centre, so each bolt feels a direct share plus a turning share. The method is always the same: move the load to the centroid of the bolts, split it into a force and a moment, find each bolt's share of both, and add them at the worst bolt. Machine frames, motor mounts, wall cranes and pipe brackets are sized this way.
prereq: You need direct shear, tension and the maximum principal and maximum shear stress theories from the chapters on stresses and theories of failure.

sections.h3: Threads, fasteners and the stress area

blocks.text: A screw thread has three diameters. The major diameter d is the largest and is the size in the name. The minor (core) diameter dc is at the thread root. The pitch diameter lies between them. Pitch p is the axial distance between neighbouring threads; lead is the axial advance in one turn (lead = p for a single-start thread).
M20 × 2.5 means a 20 mm major diameter and a 2.5 mm pitch (plain M20 means the coarse pitch). A through bolt takes a nut, a cap screw goes into a tapped hole and a stud is threaded at both ends.
A bolt in tension breaks across the threaded part, so its stress is taken on the tensile stress area:

blocks.where: A<sub>s</sub> is in mm², d is the major diameter in mm and p the pitch in mm. For M20 × 2.5, A<sub>s</sub> = (π/4)(17.65)² = 245 mm²; for M12 × 1.75, 84.3 mm²; for M16 × 2, 157 mm². Tables give the same values.

blocks.text: A bolt in shear is checked on the shank area πd²/4, or on the core area when threads cross the shear plane.

sections.h3: Initial tension and the bolt under an external load

blocks.text: A bolt is tightened before the service load arrives. The clamp force is the initial tension (preload) Pi. Many Indian textbooks take Pi = 2840d N (d in mm) for a fluid-tight joint: 56.8 kN for M20. The tightening torque is about T = 0.2 d Pi for dry steel.
When an external tensile load P is applied, the bolt stretches a little more and the clamped plates relax a little. Only a fraction C of P reaches the bolt:

blocks.where: C = k<sub>b</sub>/(k<sub>b</sub> + k<sub>c</sub>), where k<sub>b</sub> is the bolt stiffness and k<sub>c</sub> the stiffness of the clamped parts. A soft gasket makes C near 1; metal-to-metal joints give about 0.2 to 0.3. The joint opens when P reaches P<sub>i</sub>/(1 − C).

sections.h3: Eccentric load in the plane of the bolts

blocks.text: When the load lies in the plane of the joint, every bolt is in shear. The plate is taken as rigid and turns slightly about the bolt centroid G, so a bolt's moment share grows with its distance from G.

items: Find the centroid G of the bolt group (the centre of the bolt areas), not of the bracket.
Move the load P to G and add the moment M = P·e, where e is the perpendicular distance from G to the line of action.
Primary shear on every bolt: P<sub>1</sub> = P/n, parallel to P (n is the number of bolts).
Secondary shear on bolt i: P<sub>2</sub> = M·r<sub>i</sub>/Σr², perpendicular to the line from G to that bolt, in the sense of the moment.
Add P<sub>1</sub> and P<sub>2</sub> as vectors at each bolt: R = √(P<sub>1</sub>² + P<sub>2</sub>² + 2P<sub>1</sub>P<sub>2</sub> cos θ), with θ the angle between them. The largest R sizes the bolts.

sections.h3: Eccentric load in the plane of the bolt axes

blocks.text: A bracket bolted to a column face, with a load P hanging at distance e from the face, tries to tilt about its bottom edge. Each bolt stretches in proportion to its distance l from that edge, and every bolt also carries direct shear.

blocks.where: W<sub>i</sub> is the tensile load on bolt i in N; l<sub>i</sub> its distance from the tilting edge in mm; Σl² the sum over all bolts. Direct shear per bolt is P<sub>s</sub> = P/n.

blocks.text: The top bolt carries tension W and shear P<sub>s</sub> together. By the maximum principal stress theory the equivalent tensile load is P<sub>e</sub> = ½[W + √(W² + 4P<sub>s</sub>²)]; by the maximum shear stress theory the equivalent shear load is ½√(W² + 4P<sub>s</sub>²). Then A<sub>s</sub> ≥ P<sub>e</sub>/σ<sub>allow</sub>.

examples.question: A bracket is held by four bolts at the corners of a 100 mm × 200 mm rectangle (100 mm across, 200 mm high), with bolt centres at (±50, ±100) mm from the centroid G. A vertical load P = 12 kN acts downwards, 250 mm to the right of G, in the plane of the bracket. Find the largest bolt load and the bolt size for an allowable shear stress of 60 MPa on the shank.
steps: Primary shear: P<sub>1</sub> = 12 000/4 = 3000 N per bolt, downwards.
Moment about G: M = 12 000 × 250 = 3.0 × 10⁶ N·mm, clockwise.
Every bolt has r = √(50² + 100²) = 111.8 mm, so Σr² = 4 × 111.8² = 50 000 mm².
Secondary shear: P<sub>2</sub> = 3.0 × 10⁶ × 111.8/50 000 = 6708 N per bolt, square to its radius, clockwise.
At bolt (50, 100) the clockwise direction is (100, −50)/111.8, so P<sub>2</sub> = (6000, −3000) N; adding P<sub>1</sub> = (0, −3000) N gives (6000, −6000) N.
R = √(6000² + 6000²) = 8485 N. Bolt (50, −100) also gives 8485 N; the two left bolts give only 6000 N.
Shank area: A = 8485/60 = 141.4 mm², d = √(4 × 141.4/π) = 13.4 mm. Choose M16, the preferred size above it.
examples.answer: The two bolts on the load side carry 8.49 kN each; M16 bolts (shank 16 mm) are used, with a shear stress of 8485/201 = 42.2 MPa.

examples.question: A bracket is bolted to a steel column by four bolts in two rows. The bottom row is 50 mm and the top row 250 mm above the tilting edge, two bolts in each row. A load P = 10 kN hangs 300 mm from the column face. The allowable tensile stress of the bolt material is 84 MPa. Find the bolt size by the maximum principal stress theory.
steps: Direct shear: P<sub>s</sub> = 10 000/4 = 2500 N per bolt.
examples.answer: M12 bolts; the top bolts carry 5.77 kN tension and 2.5 kN shear, an equivalent 6.70 kN.

traps: Adding primary and secondary shear as numbers: 3000 + 6708 = 9708 N overstates the true 8485 N by 14 %. Add them as vectors.
Measuring r from the load point. In-plane shear uses r from the bolt centroid; the tilting bracket uses l from the tilting edge.
Using πd²/4 for a bolt in tension. Use A<sub>s</sub>: 245 mm² for M20, not 314 mm².
Forgetting the direct shear P/n on a tilting bracket. The top bolt carries tension and shear, combined by a failure theory.

quiz.q: What do M20 × 2.5 and the tensile stress area A<sub>s</sub> mean?
quiz.a: M20 × 2.5 is an ISO metric thread of 20 mm major diameter and 2.5 mm pitch. A<sub>s</sub> = (π/4)(d − 0.9382p)² is the effective area of the threaded part in tension, 245 mm² for M20.

quiz.q: Why does a preloaded bolt feel only part of an external tensile load?
quiz.a: Bolt and plates act as springs in parallel: the load stretches the bolt and unloads the plates, so the bolt takes only C = k<sub>b</sub>/(k<sub>b</sub> + k<sub>c</sub>) of it until the plates separate.

quiz.q: Four bolts lie at (±40, ±60) mm. A vertical load of 8 kN acts 150 mm to the right of the centroid. Find the largest bolt shear.
A bolt with P<sub>i</sub> = 20 kN clamps parts with C = 0.25. Find the bolt load under an external 12 kN and the load that opens the joint.
In the first worked example, why do the two left bolts carry only 6.0 kN while the right bolts carry 8.49 kN?
quiz.a: On the right the secondary shear has a 3000 N downward part that adds to the primary shear. On the left its vertical part is upwards and cancels the primary shear, leaving only the horizontal 6000 N.

quiz.q: For the tilting bracket, what happens to the top-bolt tension if the top row is moved from 250 mm to 350 mm above the tilting edge?
quiz.a: Σl² = 2(50² + 350²) = 250 000 mm², so W = 10 000 × 300 × 350/250 000 = 4200 N, down from 5769 N. Spreading the rows raises Σl² faster than l, so the worst bolt is relieved.

beyond: Not for the exam. Critical bolted joints are designed with the guideline VDI 2230, which adds joint stiffness, preload scatter and embedding losses. Torque-angle and ultrasonic tightening control preload better than a torque wrench. Search for VDI 2230 and the Junker vibration test.

figure.caption: The worked example’s bracket. The 12 kN load acts 250 mm to the right of the bolt centroid G. At the two right-hand bolts the primary shear P₁ (3.0 kN, down) and the secondary shear P₂ (6.71 kN, square to the radius) add to R = 8.49 kN; on the left they partly cancel.
